lobby.name: Ground floor — lobby and entrance hall
lobby.note: Found no rule violations — palette, props, stair cells, columns, duplicates, support and reachability all pass — so I kept the layout and only thickened it: a second chain lantern over the runner's west half, the yellow apron widened to wrap the stair foot, and planting continued along the south glass and into the north-east corner.

market.name: The Market Hall
market.note: One real fault: copper_chest carried facing=north but has no property-vocabulary entry in the brief, so both chests now go bare (their default already faces north); also set the chain-hung signs to attached=true, gave the barrow its own hanging sign, and added stall matting, a composter and a chiseled_bookshelf so all four pitches read as pitches.

workshop.name: The Copper Forge
workshop.note: Freed the copper chest — cut_copper sat directly on it, so it could never be opened — by moving it into the west work run and dropping a barrel in its place; turned the three hood stairs from south to north so the canopy hangs over the hearth instead of into the wall; tapered the flue with two cut_copper slabs, and added a tool chest by the forge and a half-stack of copper on the stock pile.

kitchen.name: The Kitchen and Brewhouse
kitchen.note: Fixed the table — its four birch_fence legs are 1.5 tall, so they stabbed up through the trapdoor top and formed the room's only impassable wall; now stripped_birch_log — and the hood, whose three closed top-half trapdoors sat buried flush under the chimney block and rendered as nothing; they now hang open as the skirt. Added a head chair at the table's west end, a lantern over the brewing bench, and a candle on the prep counter.

library.name: The Reading Room
library.note: Turned the archive chest so its front is not buried in a bookshelf and moved the decorated pot out of the stair landing's doorway; added stack-head signs, a west window seat and a third hanging lantern. [build] The east stack ran wall to wall at x=-141 and sealed the twelve floor cells between it and the stair, which the walk check caught; its south end (z=289) is now a gap you go through.

apartment_s1.name: South-landing flat A
apartment_s1.note: Fixed the one real fault - birch_shelf floated at (-147,dy3,290) with air below and only the glass wall behind it, re-mounted at (-150,dy2,290) where the smoker supports it from below and the south-west glowstone column backs it; all other 49 blocks verified against palette, props, bounds, the south-landing blocked cells, glowstone columns, bed halves, support, duplicates and a walkability trace, and left unchanged.

apartment_s2.name: Dais Flat — south-landing variant B
apartment_s2.note: Mechanically it was clean; ten pieces faced the wrong way — both dais steps rose away from the dais, the desk chair and the two window-bench seats sat with their backs to the desk and the view, the nook seats stared at the stairwell, the chiseled bookshelf's face was sealed by the shelf directly in front of it, and two barrel faces were buried against a plank and a stair — all turned round, plus a lectern in the bare north-west floor.

apartment_n1.name: North-landing flat A — the window seat
apartment_n1.note: Repaired: statue taken out of the stair bay onto the cupboard top, glow-berry vines dropped (they grow down and would curtain the west glass), lectern moved off the chiseled bookshelf's only usable face, and the boxed-in corner pot swapped with the wardrobe so no cell is sealed; fence table posts now connect.

apartment_n2.name: The Fernery
apartment_n2.note: Rules all passed; fixed a moss strand dangling in mid-air over bare floor at (-145,284) by hanging it over the potting bench, finished the moss verge that stopped one cell short of the growing bed, turned the stool to face the potting slab instead of the cauldron, and added a window seat and side table at the north glass, a chair at the lectern and a pot in the dead north-west corner.

lounge.name: The Sky Lounge
lounge.note: Cleared the planter that pinched the stair landing's only south exit to one cell, moved the west planter off the bar stool it was fusing to, dropped the bar sign to a readable height on two chains, gave the back bar a capped post and second shelf, and added two window seats to the empty north-west corner.
